propositions: The flat per-context bound of 100,000 chars has been outgrown a second time; c9f7 with 121,147 chars is refused at recovery preflight despite the product (121,147 × 22 criteria = 2.67M chars) remaining under the ratified worst-case ceiling (32 × 100k = 3.2M chars).

The root cause is conflation of two independent ceilings: a physical ceiling (context must fit in one model window) and an economic ceiling (recovery re-sends context per criterion, so total spend scales as context_chars × criteria_count).

The physical ceiling must derive from the resolved verifier model's actual context window via a model-specific accessor, not a flat constant; this requires moving MODEL_LADDER to model_classes.py and adding an own-window accessor distinct from plan_review's escalation-aware largest_window_tokens.

The economic ceiling should be explicit as _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS = 3,200,000 (the previously ratified worst case), refusing when len(context) × len(criteria) exceeds it, rather than split arbitrarily per-axis.
Refusal diagnostics must remain visible and elision-free, reporting context_chars, context_char_limit, criteria_total, recovery_input_chars, and recovery_input_char_limit.

The append-only store and d59e's pinned invariants (no comment deletion, nothing elided, criteria budget ≤ context budget) must be preserved; the two-ceiling bound unblocks re-certification while remaining interim pending the banked-verification sibling that replaces per-criterion fan-out with batching.
